draft.title: Target markets and differentiation
card: The group of customers a product is aimed at. A business picks the group by things such as age, income, interests or location.
Making a product stand out from similar products, so customers have a reason to choose it.
A business can differentiate by price (cheaper or more exclusive), quality (more durable or better made), design (look or features) or brand (name and image).
The best way to stand out depends on the target market. A group with little money may care most about price, while another group may care more about quality or design.
draft.remember: Pick the customers first, then stand out in a way that matters to them.

a.q: A business says its new skateboard is aimed at teenagers who like street skating. What are the teenagers in this case?
a.why: The teenagers are the group the skateboard is aimed at, which is its target market. A point of difference is how the product stands out, which is differentiation and a separate idea.
a.clue: Think about who the product is for.

b.q: Tariq opens a bike shop in Orange. He sells lightweight bikes made from strong, long-lasting materials to serious riders. How does he differentiate his product?
opts: By quality, as the bikes are better made
By price, as the bikes are cheaper than rivals
By design, as the bikes have a new look
By brand, as the shop has a well-known name
b.why: The bikes stand out because of lightweight, long-lasting materials, which is quality. The serious riders are his target market, but they are the customers, not the way he stands out.
b.clue: Look at what the bikes are made from.

b.best: By quality, as the bikes are better made
